quote_original: And there is no other when you say, I am!
context_before: Remember: the source of all life is I AM! We are told that the Lord will speak to man in a dream and make himself known in a vision. The word Lord may cause you to think of another, but the Hebrew word YAD HE VAU HE [pron. “YOD HEY VAV HEY”] means “I AM”!
context_after: The spirit of truth made himself known to this lady in a vision and will lead her into all things. Trained in the belief of an external God, she has o
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from The Incarnate Revelation (1969-02-20).

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1969-02-20 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: This being is immortal and within.
context_before: Man must overcome the belief in a being outside of self before the spirit of truth can come and make himself known to him.
context_after: Each time you say I am, you speak his name. When you discover this, you will know that you and God are one!
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from The Incarnate Revelation (1969-02-20).

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1969-02-20 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: Why did He become you and I?
context_after: So that we could become God. If this is true, how will we ever know it unless God’s son calls us father? I could call you Lord, God, Jehovah, or Jesus and you would deny it; but when God’s son – who was supposed to have lived 3000 [sic] years ago – stands before you who live in the 20th century, and calls you father, you cannot deny the experience. When you see David you know you are his father and he knows he is your son. Having fallen asleep, you have forgotten your true identity. But when David appears your memory will return.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from The Incarnate Revelation (1969-02-20).

quote_original: And his fatherhood is revealed when God’s son calls you father.
context_before: Man is the only cross God ever wore and his birth takes place from man’s skull, for that is where God is buried. When He awakens in you and emerges from you, it is you who awake and emerge.
context_after: Then you will tell the truth you have experienced to the world in the hope they will receive it. But whether they do or not, you will know that the sp
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from The Incarnate Revelation (1969-02-20).

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1969-02-20 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: I cannot deny the world’s unpleasantness.
context_before: And when you awaken and you and I are reunited in the one body, we will know what we have done in this adventure.
context_after: Every newspaper tells of something terrible. You rarely read a pleasant headline. If they cannot find something bad in our city, they jump across the ocean to find it. The world is built that way, yet it is moving toward a glorious divine event.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from The Incarnate Revelation (1969-02-20).

author: Neville Goddard

quote_original: So Mary is gone, taking all of her beliefs with her.
context_before: Two years ago, while in New York I learned that Mary had been killed. Walking down a dark street one night she stepped off the sidewalk and a car struck her. Her husband found her body four days later in the morgue where they kept it waiting for identification.
context_after: There is no transforming power in what the world calls death. If you are prejudiced here, you are prejudiced there. If you change the price of books h
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from The Incarnate Revelation (1969-02-20).

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1969-02-20 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: Then dare to assume you have it.
context_before: Test my words, for I know the human imagination is God. Call forth your desire by calling it forth with God’s name. Decide what you want and ask yourself what it would be like and how you would feel if it were true.
context_after: Let the people who know you now see you after your assumption. Don’t make them see you; let them see the change!
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from The Incarnate Revelation (1969-02-20).

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1969-02-20 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: No one can see I am!
context_before: There is only one source. The world calls it God. That is a lovely name, but don’t forget that God is your awareness!
context_after: They see what I tell them that I am. I walk the earth and they see that I am a man wearing a gray suit. I tell them where I live, and they know the names of my father and mother, sister and brothers; but these are only covers for the being that I am, as no one can see my true identity on this level. They only see my metamorphosis.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from The Incarnate Revelation (1969-02-20).

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1969-02-20 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: How could God lose himself when he became man?
context_before: All punctuation is man-made. Change the comma and you will see that no one can be lost.
context_after: He could not – therefore God has to redeem himself.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from The Incarnate Revelation (1969-02-20).
